paper.title: Combinatorial Pure Exploration with Full-Bandit or Partial Linear Feedback

settings.name_in_paper: Combinatorial pure exploration with full-bandit linear feedback (CPE-BL)
unmapped: Action set X subset of {0,1}^d with combinatorial structure (matroids, matchings, paths); m = max ||x||_1
Full-bandit feedback y_t = x^T(theta + eta_t) with noise vector eta_t in [-1,1]^d
Efficient maximization oracle used via Lawler's k-best procedure
settings.definition_quote: At each time step $t$, a learner pulls a super arm $x_t$ and receives a random reward (full-bandit feedback)  $y_t=x^{\top} (\theta + \eta_t )$, where $\eta_t$ is a zero-mean noise vector bounded in $[-1,1]^d$ ... There is an unknown environment vector $\theta \in \mathbb{R}^d$ with $\| \theta\|_2 \leq L$ ... we assume that the optimal $x^*$ is unique

settings.name_in_paper: Combinatorial pure exploration with partial linear feedback (CPE-PL)
unmapped: Feedback y_t = M_{x_t}(theta + eta_t) with known transformation matrices M_x (partial linear feedback)
Possibly nonlinear expected reward r(x,theta), L_p-Lipschitz in theta (Assumption 1), not necessarily observed
Existence of a known global observer set sigma with M_sigma full column rank (Assumption 2); learner knows sigma, beta_sigma and L_p
Noise vectors eta_t in [-1,1]^d (used in the definition of beta_sigma)
Offline maximization oracle for r(x, theta)
settings.definition_quote: In CPE-PL, each super arm $x \in \mathcal{X}$ is associated with a transformation matrix $M_x \in \mathbb{R}^{m_x \times d}$ ... a learner pulls a super arm $x_t$ and observes a random linear feedback  vector $y_t=M_{x_t} (\theta + \eta_t ) \in \mathbb{R}^{m_{x_t}}$ ... Meanwhile, the learner gains a random reward with expectation of $\bar{r}(x_t, \theta)$.

settings.name_in_paper: CPE-BL, (epsilon,delta)-PAC identification with sub-Gaussian noise (CLUNCB analysis)
unmapped: kappa-sub-Gaussian noise; regularized least squares with parameter iota
Complexity depends on width(X) of exchange class (Chen et al. 2014)
settings.definition_quote: We show that with a simple modification using the regularized least-square estimator, CLUCB algorithm~proposed in~\cite{Chen2014} can work for CPE-BL for general constraints ... and it is a polynomial-time $(\epsilon,\delta)$-PAC algorithm.

bound.expression: sum_i_2_to_half_d(c_0/Delta_i**2*(log(1/delta) + log(n_X) + log(log(1/Delta_i)))) + c_0*d*(alpha_pa*sqrt(m) + alpha_pa**2)/Delta_d1**2*(log(1/delta) + log(n_X) + log(log(1/Delta_d1)))

symbols.sum_i_2_to_half_d: sum over ranks i = 2, ..., floor(d/2) of super arms ordered by expected reward
symbols.Delta_i: gap between x* and the super arm with the i-th largest expected reward
symbols.Delta_d1: Delta_{d+1}, gap of the (d+1)-th best super arm
symbols.c_0: max{4L^2, 3} with L the l2 bound on theta
symbols.alpha_pa: sqrt(m d / xi_min(tilde M(lambda*_{X_sigma}))), approximation parameter computed by Algorithm 5

source.label: thm:CPE-BL
source.quote: With probability at least $1-\delta$, the \textsf{PolyALBA} algorithm (Algorithm \ref{alg:PolyALBA}) returns the best super arm $x^*$ with sample complexity O(...) where $\alpha = \sqrt{md/\xi_{\min}(\widetilde{M}(\lambda^*_{\mathcal{X}_{\sigma}}))}$.

results.notes: Both correctness and sample complexity hold w.p. >= 1-delta.

bound.expression: c_0*d*(alpha_pa*sqrt(m) + alpha_pa**2)/Delta_d1**2*(log(1/delta) + log(n_X) + log(log(1/Delta_d1))) + sum_i_2_to_half_d(c_0/Delta_i**2*(log(1/delta) + log(n_X) + log(log(1/Delta_i))))

symbols.alpha_pa: min{nu*/sqrt(d), min_i sqrt(m d / xi_min(tilde M(lambda_i)))}, with nu* the optimal value of LP_primal in Algorithm 8

conditions: X has an efficient separation oracle for its polytope (matroid, matroid intersection, s-t paths) for polynomial-time LP
tuning: distribution lambda computed by the ellipsoid-method Algorithm 8 instead of Algorithm 5

source.label: corollary:ellipsoid_method
source.quote: Let $\nu^*$ be the optimal value for $\mathrm{LP}_{\mathrm{primal}}$ obtained in Algorithm~\ref{alg:G-opt-approx}. With probability at least $1-\delta$, the \textsf{PolyALBA} algorithm (Algorithm \ref{alg:PolyALBA}) will return the best super arm $x^*$ with the expected sample complexity O(...) where $\alpha =\min\{  \frac{\nu^*}{\sqrt{d}},  \min_{i \in [n]}\sqrt{\frac{md}{\xi_{\min}(\tilde{M}(\lambda_i))}} \}$.

results.notes: Paper mixes 'with probability 1-delta' and 'expected sample complexity' (expectation over the random choice of lambda); recorded as high probability. Same form as Theorem 1 with a different alpha.

symbols.sigma_size: |sigma| <= d, size of the global observer set
symbols.beta_sigma: max over eta_i in [-1,1]^d of ||(M_sigma^T M_sigma)^{-1} sum_i M_{x_i}^T M_{x_i} eta_i||_2
symbols.L_p: Lipschitz constant of the expected reward function in theta

conditions: Assumption 1 (Lipschitz expected reward with constant L_p)

source.label: thm:GCB_ub
source.quote: With probability at least $1-\delta$, the \textsf{GCB-PE} algorithm (Algorithm \ref{alg:GCB-PE}) will return the optimal super arm $x^*$ with sample complexity $O ( \frac{|\sigma| \beta_\sigma^2 L_p^2}{\Delta_{\textup{min}}^2} \log ( \frac{ \beta_\sigma^2 L_p^2}{\Delta_{\textup{min}}^2 \delta } ) )$, where $|\sigma| \leq d$.

results.notes: Proof gives explicit constant 655 for the number of exploration rounds. Delta_min is the gap between best and second-best super arm.

symbols.H_tilde: max_e M(lambda_C)^{-1}(e,e) min{9 width(X)^2/Delta_e^2, 4 m^2/(epsilon d^2)}, lambda_C the empirical pull distribution of CLUNCB

conditions: T large enough that empirical design approximates M(lambda_C)

source.label: Corollary:CLUCB
source.quote: Let $\lambda_{\mathrm{C}} \in \triangle(\cX)$ be a distribution in which $\lambda_{\mathrm{C}}(x)$ represents the ratio that $x$ is pulled by \textsf{CLUNCB}. The total number of samples $T$ is bounded as $T = O ( d \kappa^2  \tilde{H} \log ( \frac{ d \kappa^2  m \tilde{H}/\iota + \log \delta^{-1}}{\delta} ) )$

results.notes: Holds on the 1-delta event; bound depends on the algorithm-dependent design lambda_C and proof uses an approximation step. epsilon-PAC guarantee.
